newsitem.title: USA: Deluxe Q2 results in line with year target.
newsitem.headline: Deluxe Q2 results in line with year target.

text.p: Deluxe Corp said Monday its second quarter results were in line with its previously announced target of adjusted earnings per share from operations of $2.15 a share for 1997.

Earlier, Deluxe reported second quarter earnings of $0.46 a share, even with a year ago. It earned $0.96 a share for the first six months, up from year-ago earnings of $0.69 a share after a $0.25 restructuring charge.
Deluxe reported operating earnings in 1996, before charges, of $1.90 a share.

"Our full-year earnings target remains weighted toward the end of the year, when our check printing plant consolidation efforts are expected to yield additional cost reduction benefits and when a number of new revenue-generating products and programs begin to kick in," J.A. Blanchard, chairman, said in a statement.

Blanchard said performance at Deluxe Financial Services was mixed in the second quarter. Deluxe's payment protection businesses and forms unit showed profit improvements. But the financial institution checking print operations did not meet their quarterly objective, he added.
Although Deluxe's check order units increased in the quarter, Blanchard said financial institution check printing revenues were flat.

So far, Deluxe converted 1,108 of its 13,500 financial institution customers to the new order fulfillment system, and expects to be producing more than eight million orders on the system by year-end. The company will convert all of its customers and orders to the new system by year-end 1998.

Deluxe closed manufacturing operations in six of the 11 plants now expected to close this year and 18 of the 26 total announced in January 1996. Deluxe said two plant closings have been pushed into the first quarter of 1998 and one into 1999 because of increased order volume.

Deluxe said its Deluxe Electronic Payment Systems (DEPS) continued its restructuring in the second quarter. DEPS is not expected to be profitable this year as it undergoes a major infrastructure overhaul and systems upgrade.
However, it is ahead of its original timeline for returning to profitability, Blanchard said.
Deluxe previously announced plans to sell the businesses in its Deluxe Direct market-serving unit, which includes Current Social Expressions, PaperDirect and Nelco.
